questions.prompt: What should decide how test cases are grouped into suites?
options: Purpose and run cadence, such as smoke, feature and regression
questions.explanation: Suites exist so the right tests run at the right time. Folder structure alone does not capture that.

questions.prompt: A test case can belong to more than one suite if suites are assembled with tags.
questions.explanation: Tags such as component, priority and requirement let suites be assembled without duplicating cases.

questions.prompt: Which data is a valid boundary variant for a field that accepts 1 to 20 characters?
questions.explanation: 20 characters is the upper boundary. 10 is typical; empty is an invalid partition.

questions.prompt: Which belong in documented test data for a feature? Select all that apply.
options: The data values and where they come from
How to reset or recreate the data
Which tests rely on which records
questions.explanation: Documented data and reset steps make runs reproducible. Personal passwords should never be in documentation.

questions.prompt: A developer offers a full production database copy for realistic reporting tests. What is the best response?
options: Ask for masked or synthetic data that keeps the relevant volume and relationships, with approval
Accept only if the testers sign something
questions.explanation: Unmasked personal production data breaks privacy rules. Masked or synthetic data keeps realism without exposure.

questions.prompt: Which suite is intended to run after every build to check critical functions only?
questions.explanation: Smoke suites are short and fast; regression is broader and slower.

questions.prompt: Regression tests pass on a fresh environment but fail on the second run. What is the most likely data issue?
options: Tests change shared data (e.g. create fixed IDs or consume records) without resetting it
questions.explanation: Non-repeatable tests leave state behind. Documenting and automating data set-up and clean-up makes runs repeatable.

questions.prompt: Your regression suite has 900 cases, takes 3 days manually, and 40% have never failed or been linked to risk. What is the best way to improve it?
options: Tag cases by risk and requirement, review them, and split into a smaller high-risk suite run every release and a wider suite run less often
questions.explanation: Risk-based tagging and splitting keeps important coverage while managing effort. A test that never failed may still protect critical behaviour.

questions.prompt: You test a 'Full name' field. Which set is the best minimum coverage?
options: A typical name, a single character, the maximum length, an apostrophe name, an accented name, leading and trailing spaces, an empty value
questions.explanation: The set combines typical, boundary, special and invalid values. One value or random volume misses systematic coverage.
